**Thesis.** Carpenter grows operating income from $702M in FY2026 to about $1.13B in FY2029 on pricing, mix and the Athens brownfield capacity, and converts it to $1.9B of FCF over the period; at a mid-cycle 17x EV/EBIT that is worth about $405 in mid-2029, and about $389 after weighting a 30% chance of an aerospace destock.

**Variant view.** Both reads are off. The earnings engine held through a maintenance quarter: SAO adjusted margin was 37.7% against a 37.8% record, structural and distribution aerospace bookings rose 49% year over year, and management says pricing is still rising on LTA and spot business. So the de-rating overstates the damage. But the FY2029 target needs record margins, a fast brownfield ramp and no aerospace hiccup, and earnings at peak margins deserve a mid-cycle multiple. On $1.13B of FY2029 operating income at 17x, the stock is worth about $405, roughly 14.5% a year: good, not cheap enough for a cyclical at a record margin.

**Catalysts.**

- Q2 FY2027 results (Around January 28, 2027 (estimated from the prior-year release))
- Q3 FY2027 results (Around April 28, 2027)
- FY2027 results and FY2028 outlook (Around July 29, 2027)
- Latrobe collective bargaining agreement expires (450 production employees) (July 31, 2027)
- Athens, Alabama brownfield expansion comes online and qualifies (Early FY2028 (July-December 2027))
- New long-term agreements with engine and structural customers (FY2027-FY2028)

**Pre-mortem** (written at decision time).

- The aerospace supply chain destocked in 2027: Boeing and engine programs missed rate targets, distributors cut orders, and spot pricing on non-LTA business stopped rising. FY2028 operating income fell below FY2027 and the stock was valued as a cyclical at the top. — watch: Two straight quarters of lower sequential aerospace bookings, or management dropping 'accelerating demand' language; distribution sub-market bookings down year over year
- New premium-melt capacity from ATI, Haynes (Acerinox) and imports arrived as Carpenter's brownfield came online, and LTA renewals were priced flat. SAO margins fell from 38% to about 30%. — watch: SAO adjusted operating margin below 35% in any quarter, or LTA renewals described as flat
- Execution slipped after the CEO's death: the brownfield ran late and over budget, a planned outage became an unplanned one at Reading, and senior turnover continued. FY2027 missed guidance and the FY2029 target was withdrawn. — watch: Q2 or Q3 FY2027 operating income below the quarterly guide, FY2027 capex above $375M, or another senior officer departure
- Management kept buying back stock with borrowed money while FCF was weak (Q1 FY2027 repurchases were at about $553 a share) and entered a downturn with a drawn revolver. — watch: Revolver borrowings above $200M at a quarter end while repurchases continue

**Kill criteria.**

- FY2027 operating income below $800M in the FY2027 results release (check by 2027-08-31) — open
- FY2029 operating income target withdrawn, or its low end cut below $1.1B (check by 2027-08-31) — open
- SAO adjusted operating margin (excluding surcharge) below 33% for two consecutive quarters (check by 2027-11-15) — open
- Athens brownfield expansion not shipping qualified material by June 30, 2028 (check by 2028-08-31) — open

**Probability claims.**

- 80%: Carpenter's operating income for Q2 FY2027 (quarter ending December 31, 2026), as reported in its earnings release, is at least $192.0 million. (resolves by 2027-02-15)
- 60%: Carpenter's FY2027 operating income (year ending June 30, 2027), as reported in its FY2027 earnings release, is at least $850.0 million. (resolves by 2027-08-31)
- 50%: Carpenter's FY2027 free cash flow (or adjusted free cash flow) as reported in its FY2027 earnings release is at least $400.0 million. (resolves by 2027-08-31)
- 70%: In its FY2027 earnings release or call materials, Carpenter states an FY2029 operating income target whose low end is at least $1.2 billion. (resolves by 2027-08-31)
- 45%: Carpenter's FY2027 cash flow statement shows purchases of common stock of at least $400 million. (resolves by 2027-08-31)

**What would change the view.**

- More bullish: Q2 FY2027 operating income at or above $197M with sequential bookings growth and new LTAs disclosed at higher prices
- More bullish: the same facts at a price near $256, where the weighted value implies 15% a year on the 3-year rule, or evidence that rules out a halving of operating income before FY2029
- More bearish: Q2 FY2027 operating income below $185M, an FY2027 guide cut, or SAO adjusted margin below 35%
- More bearish: a brownfield delay past June 2028 or FY2027 capex above $375M

**Independent review: grade B** (evidence 4, valuation 3, variant view 3, risk 4, calibration 3). Counter-case: Carpenter is a cyclical at the top: the call's own bear still has FY2029 operating income above FY2026's record and margins more than double the FY2012-FY2019 average, so every weighted scenario assumes the best earnings in the company's 137 years persist, while the last two downturns took operating income down 78% and then below zero. The near-term evidence is already turning: SAO missed its own Q1 segment guide ($216.3M against $218-222M), the Q2 consolidated guide ($192-197M) is below the Q1 guide ($195-200M), defense orders fell, the CEO died, eight Street targets were cut 25-30%, and management spent $133.9M buying stock at about $553 while free cash flow was negative. Weight the $120 deep bear at even 15% and the value falls toward $360, under 10% a year, which is a Watch with a negative bias, not a positive one.

**Response.** Fixed: the horizon is now stated both ways (13.0% a year on the 3-year rule, 15.0% on the actual 2.62 years to June 2029); the bear weight is now justified by the modeled event (a pricing stall as the industry adds capacity) and the deep bear is named as unweighted, with its effect (15% weight taken pro rata gives about $349, about 9% a year on the rule); the Street rating counts, median target ($450), Q1 guide (operating income $196.4M was inside the $195-200M guide; only SAO missed its segment guide), October 22 close ($292.26, -20.6%), target-cut dates, trailing EV/EBIT (18.8x), FY2026 Q4 revenue miss and the EPS note were corrected. Partly accepted: the counter-case is the reason the stance is Watch and not Own even though the weighted value meets the hurdle on the actual horizon. Not accepted: a negative bias. Q1 operating income rose 28% with SAO margin within 0.1 point of its record, the full-year and FY2029 targets were reaffirmed, commercial aerospace bookings rose 49% year over year, and the balance sheet has no maturity before 2034, so the evidence for a halving within three years is the industry's history, not current data. The kill criteria (Q2 operating income below $185M, SAO margin below 35%, two quarters of falling aerospace bookings) are where that history would first show.

**Data notes.** Price is the 2026-11-17 committed close. The StockAnalysis page implies a 2026-11-18 close of about $272.04, not yet in the committed series. FCF after dividends accrues as cash in the model rather than buying back stock at an assumed price. Buybacks below the case value would add to per-share value in the base and bull; buybacks above it (as in Q1 FY2027 at about $553) subtract. Sensitivity: each 1x of exit EV/EBIT is worth about $22 a share in the base ($1,130M / 50.6M shares); each $50M of FY2029 operating income is worth about $17 at 17x. A deep bear (FY2029 operating income $520M, about the FY2025 level, at 10x) would be about $120. Exit multiples were tested with python3 -m capital.multiples: Carpenter's own EV/EBIT p10 11.2x, p25 15.6x, median 22.5x, p75 29.8x (94 months); at October 31, 2026 ATI was 26.7x and Howmet 30.3x. The SIC group has no other covered names, so ATI and HWM were captured as named peers. Revenue includes raw-material surcharge (FY2026 $596.7M of $3,124.2M), which moves with nickel and cobalt prices; operating income is the cleaner driver.
